intervention_description: Both OPUS randomised arms merged into a single cohort at long-term follow-up because the aims were unrelated to treatment assignment
Whole birth cohort psychosis cases identified from national registers; no allocation

Whole population detained in the high secure State Hospital between 25 Aug 1992 and 13 Aug 1993
Subgroup with definite or probable schizophrenia by Feighner criteria

intervention_description: Cognitive behavioural social recovery therapy targeting activity and personal goals added to TAU
Treatment as usual: case management from a secondary mental health care team; no psychological therapy

Non-affective psychosis subgroup of the TAU arm

intervention_description: Affective psychosis subgroup of the SRT arm
Affective psychosis subgroup of the TAU arm

Best available vocational rehabilitation provided by the Danish national job centres

Patients who suspended work or study activity at illness onset (denominator for the return-to-activity outcome)

Recurrent/relapsing episode cohort: prior diagnosis of schizophrenia presenting with a new episode or relapse

Employment analysis restricted to patients not receiving a disability pension at baseline: 'In the analysis of employment we omitted the patients who were receiving disability pension at baseline, 71/362 (19.6%), because their employment status could not have changed' (Results, Employment, p. 268).

Patients whose final 3-year ICD-10 research diagnosis was schizophrenia (first-episode schizophrenia, FES), among the 420 who completed 3-year follow-up. A post-hoc diagnostic split of one recruited sample, so `subgroup` rather than a separate cohort: the split is made at 3 years on the longitudinal course, not at recruitment.

Patients whose final 3-year ICD-10 research diagnosis was mania with psychotic features (first-episode mania with psychotic features, FEMP), among the 420 who completed 3-year follow-up. Post-hoc diagnostic split of the same recruited sample as arm `fes`.

10 months of vocational rehabilitation in competitive workplaces, work placements and sheltered workshops with formalised collaboration between mental health and vocational services, augmented for 6 months by cognitive remediation (three counties) or work-focused CBT techniques (three counties). Both allocation groups are merged in every whole-cohort figure. No non-augmented control arm exists.

The 69 of 148 JUMP participants (45 CBT, 24 CR) who gave separate consent for extraction of health and welfare register data for the cost-effectiveness analysis. The subgroup criterion (consent to register linkage) is NOT itself employment related; the cohort-level vocational-service restriction still applies. The authors report no significant difference between consenters and decliners on diagnosis, age, sex, DDD, symptoms, education, previous work experience or 2-year employment outcome.

PAFIP: three-year specialised early intervention programme (low-dose antipsychotic medication with side-effect monitoring, patient and family psychoeducation, cognitive behavioural interventions, 'support for functional recovery based on return to normal daily activities (work/study)'), delivered to every participant; no allocation. mayoralvanson2019 adds that 'PAFIP has close social worker follow-up, intervention, and coordination with occupational and employment resources, aimed at getting out patients back into the labour market as soon as possible' (p. 1188). Recorded as provenance for applicability: the care received includes employment support, which is not an eligibility restriction.

OnTrackNY coordinated specialty care: multidisciplinary team (team leader, primary clinicians, outreach and recruitment coordinator, supported education and employment specialist, prescriber, nurse) delivering evidence-based psychosocial interventions and medication to every participant for an expected average of two years; no allocation. The supported education and employment specialist is part of the care received and is recorded as provenance for applicability.

The training/cross-validation split used by basaraba2023 for model development: 1038 of the 1298 OnTrackNY clients in 19 of the 20 sites, with a holdout test set of about 20 per cent reserved for external validation. Same OnTrackNY care as the cohort arm. Coded subgroup rather than cohort because it is a split of the report's own recruited sample, not the whole of it; the split is a statistical device and is not employment-related.

benson2022's relapse cohort: veterans with at least one schizophrenia-related relapse (inpatient stay or emergency department visit with a schizophrenia diagnosis) in the 12-month pre-index period, 16,866 of the 119,343, of whom 16,862 were propensity-score matched 1:1 to the nonrelapse cohort. No intervention is assigned; care is whatever the VHA delivered. Selected on relapse history, which is clinical and not employment-related.

benson2022's nonrelapse cohort: veterans with no schizophrenia-related relapse in the 12-month pre-index period, 102,477 of the 119,343, of whom 16,862 were propensity-score matched 1:1 to the relapse cohort. No intervention is assigned. Matching discards 85 per cent of the eligible nonrelapse veterans, so this arm is not a whole recruited cohort.

intervention_name: Individual placement and support (IPS) plus treatment as usual
intervention_description: Six months of IPS delivered by a vocational specialist embedded in the EPPIC clinical team, in addition to standard EPPIC treatment

Treatment as usual: referral to external government-contracted employment agencies, plus standard EPPIC treatment (medical management, out-patient case management, group programme, peer and family support)

Both randomised arms merged: the 18-month sample analysed by clarke2023 contains 54 participants from the vocational (IPS) arm and 46 from TAU (clarke2023 Table 4, p. 775), with treatment group entered only as a covariate. Half the merged cohort therefore received six months of IPS.

Whole recruited cohort: consecutive acute admissions to two Chicago hospitals, followed naturalistically at approximately 2, 4.5, 7.5, 10, 15 and 20 years. No allocation. No whole-cohort employment count is reported in either F04 report, so this row carries no result.
Patients with schizophrenia prescribed antipsychotic medication at the 20-year follow-up assessment, irrespective of earlier medication status. Naturalistic, not allocated.
Patients with schizophrenia not prescribed antipsychotic medication at the 20-year follow-up assessment, irrespective of earlier medication status. Naturalistic, not allocated.
Whole recruited cohort of 150 out-patients with severe mental illness attending one public hospital; observational, no allocation and no vocational intervention

Participants at the 20-year follow-up with complete data and a 10-year consensus diagnosis of schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder (n=80) or bipolar disorder (n=48); no vocational intervention was delivered by the study
Participants at the 20-year follow-up whose 10-year consensus diagnosis was schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder; no vocational intervention was delivered by the study
Participants at the 20-year follow-up whose 10-year consensus diagnosis was bipolar disorder with psychosis; no vocational intervention was delivered by the study
Therapeutic-community occupational rehabilitation; every resident was allocated at baseline to a hospital-based workshop, sheltered employment or supported employment

headspace Early Psychosis programme: community early-intervention care by a multidisciplinary team, with vocational support and embedded Individual Placement and Support workers as one of 16 core service components, delivered at 15 headspace centres in six clusters

Care as received in Danish child and adolescent psychiatric services; one constituent study (TEA) randomised participants to quetiapine extended release or aripiprazole, and all of its participants are included

Whole first-admission incidence cohort followed on usual sectorised catchment-area psychiatric care for 27-31 years; no allocation. Occupational status could only be read from charts for patients still followed by the catchment-area service, which is loss of ascertainment rather than an employment-related restriction of the denominator (D12.3c).

intervention_name: Portable cognitive games (Nintendo Brain Age-2) plus the participant's vocational rehabilitation services and a weekly goal-setting group
intervention_description: Hand-held Nintendo DS running Brain Age-2, used as a face-valid sham control that participants could take home; vocational rehabilitation services were unrelated to randomisation and freely accessible to both arms.

intervention_name: Laboratory-based cognitive remediation (Posit Science Brain Fitness and Insight) plus the participant's vocational rehabilitation services and a weekly goal-setting group
intervention_description: Targeted auditory and visual discrimination and memory training performed on site in a 'Cog Lab' with a monitor present; vocational rehabilitation services were unrelated to randomisation and freely accessible to both arms.
Whole recruited cohort of PEPP clients who consented to the long-term follow-up study, treated in a specialised early intervention programme; no allocation.

Whole recontacted follow-up cohort of former NIMH CTNB research volunteers; no allocation. The analysed denominator is restricted on employment-related grounds: 'Those who reported they were “retired” (n = 4) or for whom employment status was not able to be determined (n = 1) at follow-up were not included in the cohort' (Methods 2.1, p. 2). Removing retirees removes people who are by definition not employed, so the printed 45.2% sits on a denominator conditioned on labour-force status; the exclusion of the 1 undetermined case is ordinary missingness and is not the reason for this classification.

Whole register cohort of first-episode psychotic disorder in the Central Denmark Region under routine care; no allocation. The exclusion of individuals receiving a disability pension at baseline defines the study population itself and is therefore recorded at cohort level as employment_selection_status = selected, not as a further analytic restriction here.
Whole treated epidemiological cohort audited from EPPIC files; specialised first-episode psychosis care for up to 18 months, no allocation.

Both randomised EIDP conditions merged into a single analysed sample. The 449 are the participants from six of the eight sites who joined the supplemental economic study, consented to SSA data matching, were verified, and had a Social Security Disability Analysis File record; 35 were dropped for having no SSI or SSDI record and 3 for dying before 2000.

Supported employment delivered by employment specialists on multidisciplinary teams meeting frequently to coordinate employment and clinical services, aiming at placement in competitive jobs meeting career preferences, with job search beginning soon after entry and supports throughout.

intervention_name: Usual services, alone or with unenhanced vocational rehabilitation
intervention_description: Coded control_active rather than control_tau because the control condition 'was defined as either usual services alone or usual services plus unenhanced vocational rehabilitation services', so part of the arm received a vocational service.

High-fidelity IPS supported employment from a three-person vocational team alongside usual mental health treatment, with annual fidelity assessment. The 51 of 68 result uses the whole allocated arm as its denominator; every other analysis in this report is restricted to the 51 who obtained competitive work, which is selection on the outcome and yields no employment proportion.
Whole recruited cohort of an observational early intervention service; no allocation. 232 screened, 174 met the enrolment criteria.

The 150 of the 198 enrolled who were diagnosed with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder; 'Participants with nonschizophrenia diagnoses were excluded for this report in order to employ the same eligibility criteria as the NH study.' A diagnostic subgroup of a randomised trial whose two case-management arms were merged, so it is not a whole recruited cohort and takes arm_type subgroup.

Men among the 756 cases. Results for men and women are a post-hoc split of one recruited register cohort, not two recruited samples, so they are subgroup arms rather than separate cohorts. No combined-sex employment rate is printed anywhere in the report, which is why there is no whole-cohort arm.
Women among the 756 cases; see the men arm.

Both allocation groups of the RAISE-ETP cluster-randomised trial (NAVIGATE coordinated specialty care and usual community care) analysed together, with treatment group entered as a moderator and clustering by site accounted for. employment_targeted_intervention is `unclear` because this report does not describe the intervention components at all, referring to the parent trial reports; the experimental programme is widely reported to include a supported employment and education component, which cannot be established from this source either way.

intervention_name: EYE-2 (Early Youth Engagement, version 2) plus standardised EIP
intervention_description: Team-based motivational engagement intervention delivered over the whole follow-up alongside standardised EIP, addressing engagement through a motivational therapeutic alliance focused on patient treatment goals, broad systemic social support, and psychoeducation using the EYE-2 booklet series and website. Not an employment intervention, although its goal-focused alliance can encompass socio-occupational goals.

intervention_name: Standardised stand-alone early intervention in psychosis (sEIP)
intervention_description: Standardised stand-alone EIP comprising early detection, assertive engagement, work with diagnostic uncertainty, positive risk-taking, person, family and recovery focus, and NICE-recommended medication, cognitive-behavioural, family, physical and vocational interventions. Note that vocational interventions are part of standard care in BOTH arms.
Whole-population register cohort under usual Danish health and welfare provision; no allocation and no study intervention.
Whole national register cohort of first hospitalisations for schizophrenia under usual Finnish health and welfare provision; no allocation and no study intervention.
Whole national register cohort of first hospitalisations for other nonaffective psychosis under usual Finnish health and welfare provision; no allocation and no study intervention.

The two early-intervention allocations of the JCEP trial merged: 2 years of EI followed by 2 years of standard care (n = 120) and 4 years of EI (n = 120). The third allocation, 4 years of standard care (n = 120), was excluded from the analysis. This is a post-randomisation selection on treatment received, so the 240 is NOT a whole recruited cohort and cannot enter the prevalence intercept (SAP 2.1). arm_type is subgroup rather than intervention because the unit merges two distinct allocations.

intervention_name: Individual Placement and Support (IPS-Y) plus adherence therapy, added to standard care
intervention_description: 12-month IPS delivered to IPS-Y fidelity (rated 88 to 104 of 125 over the trial), with an add-on of up to eight adherence therapy sessions based on motivational interviewing integrated into the IPS meetings. Explicitly an employment, education and training intervention.

intervention_name: Treatment as usual in an outpatient psychiatric service
intervention_description: Individually tailored care in a low-threshold interdisciplinary outpatient mental health service for young adults aged 16-35, combining medication, psychoeducation, psychological therapies, family intervention, social work and general support. Social workers and counselling staff refer patients to traditional vocational rehabilitation programmes, so the control arm has a vocational pathway although not IPS.

intervention_name: Individual Placement and Support (IPS-Y) plus adherence therapy, education/training subsample
intervention_description: The IPS arm restricted to the education/training subsample. Section 3.4 defines the subsample as 'Excluding all participants who never received education or training during the follow-up period', which is a restriction on an outcome-related event occurring after randomisation, so the comparison with tau_edu is no longer protected by randomisation.
The TAU arm restricted to the education/training subsample, defined as in ips_edu.

The whole recruited cohort of 549, within which 64 attended the less intensive case management (LICM) programme and 485 did not. Assignment was by clinician judgement on symptoms and adherence, not randomisation. LICM targeted engagement and medication adherence, not employment. NO whole-cohort employment count is recorded against this arm: see unresolved_queries.md U9, because the only route to one is a sum across the two stage subgroups, which have different arm_ids and different denominators and so cannot be named as components under D12.2.
Early-stage subgroup: participants with one or fewer previous psychotic relapses. A post-hoc split of the single recruited cohort, combining LICM and non-LICM participants.
Later-stage subgroup: participants with more than one previous psychotic relapse. A post-hoc split of the single recruited cohort, combining LICM and non-LICM participants.

Early-stage participants not attending LICM. Office-based hospital care, non-assertive engagement, no home visits, monthly to three-monthly contact. A few received isolated programme components (accompanied transport 5.36%, help accessing disability benefits 1.86%, medicine delivery 0.41%); none received the home-visit component.

intervention_name: Less intensive case management (LICM) led by community health workers
intervention_description: Early-stage participants attending LICM: weekly to monthly home visits by a community health worker acting as case manager, with psychoeducation, medication adherence management, appointment arrangement, accompanied transport and facilitated access to disability benefits, supervised by two programme coordinators and a hospital team. Not an employment intervention; employment was used as a proxy for social functioning.
Later-stage participants not attending LICM; see early_nonlicm.

intervention_name: Less intensive case management (LICM) led by community health workers
intervention_description: Later-stage participants attending LICM; see early_licm.
Whole recruited cohort receiving routine psychiatric outpatient treatment at two private hospitals; no allocation and no study intervention
Whole recruited cohort receiving routine early intervention care across 14 NHS England early intervention services; naturalistic, no allocation
Whole recruited cohort followed on an FEP Integrated Care Pathway in NHS Greater Glasgow & Clyde; non-randomised prospective study, no allocation

Whole recruited cohort followed in NHS Glasgow and NHS Edinburgh mental health services; no allocation. The analysed denominator is restricted only by outcome availability, which is attrition under D12.3c, so the arm-level analysis selection is none even though the cohort-level recruitment status is unclear
Whole first-admission cohort followed naturalistically; pharmacotherapy plus psychotherapeutic and early psychosocial intervention as clinically indicated; no allocation

Whole recruited cohort receiving standard treatment during follow-up; no allocation. n_entered is blank because the size of the recruited Helsinki Early Psychosis Study cohort is never printed; 67 had baseline cognitive data and 54 had both baseline cognitive and 1-year clinical data

Free culturally adapted ACT: two to three community or home visits per week, clinical assessment and crisis intervention, psychosocial assistance, supportive counselling, family support including setting goals for employment, functional assistance, and 2-hour monthly family psychoeducation for 12 months. The team included a part-time employment specialist, so the intervention is employment-targeted and no trial-derived whole-cohort row may be created.

Existing '686 program' community mental health services free of charge: outpatient psychiatric visits every 1-3 months and home visits by public health professionals every 1-3 months with free psychotropic medication. To ensure delivery, the study team also made a monthly telephone call and a 3-monthly home visit over the 12-month follow-up.
Whole treated-incidence cohort of an early psychosis service; no allocation. Up to two years of comprehensive case management with assertive outreach.
First-generation migrants, i.e. young people born outside Australia; a post-hoc split of the one recruited cohort by country of birth.
Young people born in Australia, including second-generation migrants, whom the authors state could not be identified separately; a post-hoc split of the one recruited cohort by country of birth.
Whole recruited sample; all 53 completed the same prevocational training group before baseline. No allocation and no comparator.

Employed group (EG): the 19 participants who obtained any kind of paid work for at least 30 days during follow-up. Defined BY the outcome, so it is a post-hoc outcome-defined subgroup and can support no prevalence.
Usual vocational services enhanced by a half-day workshop for vocational specialists on cognitive impairment and job-relevant coping strategies, plus consultation calls every one to three months.

intervention_name: Thinking Skills for Work (TSW) plus Enhanced Vocational Rehabilitation
intervention_description: The same enhanced vocational services plus manualised cognitive remediation: about 24 hours of Cogpack computer exercises with strategy coaching and taught self-management strategies, delivered by a cognitive specialist integrated into the vocational team.

Manualised CBT-informed group programme targeting defeatist beliefs about work, four modules of two sessions, delivered weekly in groups of two to three alongside a four-month work therapy placement that both arms received.

Time-matched active control: weekly 45-minute participant-led support and discussion about work-related issues, with no curriculum and no personalised work feedback, alongside the same four-month work therapy placement.

Whole randomised RADAR cohort with both allocation groups combined, as the report itself does: 126 allocated to supported gradual antipsychotic dose reduction and discontinuation and 127 to maintenance antipsychotic treatment. The experimental intervention is a medication regimen, not an employment intervention.
Participants with at least one relapse of any severity during the 24-month trial. A POST-RANDOMISATION subgroup defined by an event occurring after allocation.
Participants with no relapse during the 24-month trial. A POST-RANDOMISATION subgroup defined by an event occurring after allocation.
Whole NIRP follow-up cohort; no allocation. Participants received routine community mental health care at 24 Italian university psychiatric clinics or mental health departments

intervention_name: Cognitive remediation therapy using JCORES plus bridging sessions
intervention_description: 24 computerised cognitive training sessions and 12 group bridging sessions over 3 months in a psychiatric day care, delivered as a stand-alone cognitive rehabilitation intervention; bridging sessions explicitly addressed preparing for employment and workplace difficulties

intervention_name: Morpheus multidisciplinary vocational intervention within OPUS
intervention_description: Supported employment: a municipal employment-unit social worker with schizophrenia expertise plus an OPUS occupational therapist, delivering vocational training, job coaching, a 6-week group therapy programme and direct employer engagement alongside 2 years of OPUS; started at a median of 183.5 days after OPUS inclusion

Municipal job-centre guidance, education and training, standardised across a broad range of clients and not adapted for schizophrenia; the report states it may have included IPS in some municipalities and that the content received was not recorded

Two years of multidisciplinary integrative treatment in one department: second-generation antipsychotics, individual psychotherapy, metacognitive and group therapy, Cogpack cognitive remediation, art therapy and family involvement; social and vocational rehabilitation services were offered as needed

Full-time employment specialists from a Disability Employment Service provider co-located with two community mental health clinic case management teams, delivering the IPS model under a formal partnership, March 2006 to February 2013
All 1987 Finnish Birth Cohort members diagnosed with a nonaffective psychotic disorder in 2004-2007; no allocation and no intervention beyond routine Finnish services
Cohort members whose diagnosis was schizophrenia (ICD-10 F20, n=68) or schizoaffective disorder (F25, n=18); a diagnostic subgroup of the 288, not a separately recruited sample

intervention_name: Cognitive remediation (Cogpack) plus Individual Placement and Support
intervention_description: 32 individualised one-hour computerised cognitive remediation sessions with Cogpack over 4 months, one to two per week, added to IPS supported employment delivered by a five-technician IPS team
IPS supported employment alone: rapid individualised competitive job search by employment specialists integrated with community mental health teams, continuous job support, no cognitive remediation

intervention_name: Group occupational therapy plus individualized occupational therapy (GOT + IOT)
intervention_description: Approximately three months of inpatient occupational therapy from hospitalisation to discharge, with more than half the OT time given to one-to-one goal-oriented IOT combining motivational interviewing, self-monitoring, individualised visits, craft activities with individualised coaching, individualised psychoeducation and discharge planning

Standard activity-oriented group occupational therapy already implemented at each site: physical fitness, craft activities, cooking, music, recreation and psychoeducation, with therapist assistance only on request

Whole recruited cohort of the Parachute early-intervention programme: five years of continuously available psychosocial and family support from small multidisciplinary FEP teams, with deliberately cautious low-dose short-course antipsychotic use. Not randomised and not employment-targeted, so the SAP 2.1 allocation safeguards do not arise.

Standalone community multidisciplinary EIP teams operating to IRIS guidelines: client-to-care-coordinator ratio 1:15, weekly contact, psychological and family therapy delivered within the team, 3 years of treatment. Allocation is by home address, since only 6 of the 12 clinical commissioning groups funded an EIP service; there is no randomisation. ANALYSIS-LEVEL SELECTION, recorded here and NOT at cohort level: the employment result is 'the proportion of those unemployed at start of follow-up who became employed during follow-up' (Methods, p. 3), so the analysed denominator, not the recruitment, is restricted on baseline employment. The cohort itself carries no employment-related recruitment criterion and is coded employment_selection_status = none.

Standard community mental health team care: caseload per care coordinator at least 1:30, psychological and family therapy only after referral to a separate service with a waiting list of several months, treatment for the duration of the acute illness (6-9 months for first-episode psychosis) and then discharge. No vocational component is described. Same analysis-level restriction to those unemployed at the start of follow-up as the EIP arm.

intervention_name: Two-pronged vocational intervention: individual placement and support (IPS) with supported education, or the Workplace Fundamentals Module job-retention programme
intervention_description: Whole consenting sample of EIPS clients who used a vocational intervention; no allocation, the occupational therapist decided which prong applied. IPS for those without a productive role, the 8-week group Workplace Fundamentals Module for those with one; 21 used IPS alone, 9 WFM alone and 9 both. The analysed denominator of 34 is everyone followed up and carries no employment-related restriction, so analysis_selection_status = none: the loss of 5 is attrition (D12.3c), not selection. The employment-related selection is at COHORT level (entry into the vocational service). employment_targeted_intervention = yes, so this whole-cohort row cannot enter the prevalence intercept under SAP section 2.1 even if the cohort gate were passed.

intervention_name: Individual placement and support (IPS) with supported education
intervention_description: Post-hoc split of the single recruited sample by baseline vocational status, not a separately recruited group and not an allocated arm (D12.5). 21 of the 39 consenters were unoccupied at baseline and were offered IPS; 16 of those 21 were followed up and form the denominator of the attainment result. The restriction is on baseline employment status and attaches to the analysed denominator, which is why it is recorded here rather than at cohort level.

Whole consecutively enrolled cohort of under-18 admissions with an ICD-10 discharge diagnosis of schizophrenia in 2006, followed to a single interview about 10 years later under routine care; no allocation and no study intervention. The analysed denominator of 62 is the surviving interviewees; the 53 not interviewed were lost to follow-up (48 discontinued phone numbers, 5 refusals), which is attrition and not an employment-related restriction (D12.3c).

intervention_name: Supported employment programmes scoring below the JiSEF 90/91 cut-off (mean 80.1, SD 6.5; 7 programmes)
intervention_description: Non-randomised subgroup: participants are grouped by the fidelity score of the agency they had already entered, not by any allocation, so arm_type = subgroup rather than control_active. Services were heavily weighted to agency-based group work (83 per cent of service hours). analysis_selection_status = unclear because 93 clients met the inclusion criteria during the recruitment window and only 51 were analysed, with no explanation in the article text; the flow diagram that would say why is in an online supplement not held, so absence of a further employment-related restriction on the analysed denominator cannot be established (silence is not evidence of absence).

intervention_name: Supported employment programmes scoring at or above the JiSEF 90/91 cut-off (mean 100.8, SD 5.3; 6 programmes)
intervention_description: Non-randomised subgroup defined by agency fidelity score, not by allocation. Services were balanced across outreach (29 per cent), agency-based individual (36 per cent) and agency-based group services (32 per cent), with more outreach job development before a job was obtained. Same unexplained 51-of-93 analysed denominator as the low-fidelity arm.

intervention_name: Integrated supported employment (ISE): IPS plus a 10-session work-related social skills training programme
intervention_description: IPS delivered to the eight implementation principles, plus the manualised 10-session work-related social skills training programme in the first 3 months before job seeking, plus follow-up generalisation support. Fidelity 64-67 of 75 (85-89 per cent). The analysed denominator is the whole randomised arm under intent-to-treat, so no further analytic restriction applies; the employment-related selection (unemployed at entry and a desire to work) is at cohort level.

Job development and placement, ongoing work support, coordination of vocational services with multidisciplinary teams, indefinite services and participant job choice, delivered by the same three employment specialists as the ISE arm. Fidelity 65-68 of 75 (87-91 per cent). An active vocational comparator, not treatment as usual.

Comprehensive vocational assessment, situational assessment with the Workshop Behavior Checklist and prevocational training for later upgrading to competitive employment, provided by mental health centre staff delivering sheltered vocational training. An active vocational comparator ('train then place'), so control_active rather than control_tau.
